Command: Take the four species on Tabernacles
Summary: On the first day of Tabernacles, Israel takes the fruit of goodly trees, palm branches, boughs of thick trees, and willows of the brook, and rejoices before the LORD.
Commandment: On the first day of Tabernacles, take the four species — goodly fruit, palm branches, thick boughs, and brook willows — and rejoice before the LORD.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The branches in hand made the harvest joy visible and tangible through the feast week. Debated: some see the commanded observance fulfilled as shadow (Colossians 2:16-17); others keep feasts voluntarily as memorial, not as binding command. The site does not settle whether observance continues.
Purpose: To rehearse God's saving acts at appointed seasons (Leviticus 23); Paul calls Christ our Passover (1 Corinthians 5:7).
